newsitem.title: USA: Friends line up to pay respects to Tsongas.
newsitem.headline: Friends line up to pay respects to Tsongas.

text.p: Hundreds of mourners lined up on the sidewalk in front of former Sen. Paul Tsongas' house Tuesday to pay respects to a Washington politician they said never forgot his hometown.

Friends and admirers were welcomed inside from the cold, into the Tsongas living room, past easels holding black-and-white photographs of the senator who died Saturday at age 55 from pneumonia associated with complications from an earlier bout against bone cancer.

The son of a Greek immigrant father and an American mother, Tsongas rose from being a city councillor for this depressed mill town to representing Massachusetts in the House of Representatives and the Senate before unsuccessfully running for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1992.

"He was very honest and he always helped the people he grew up with," remembered Ernest Kotsopoulos, a retired software engineer and a life-long acquaintance. "Wherever he went, whether it was in Washington or whether he came back from his Peace Corps job, he made a point of really concentrating on the greater Lowell area."
About 30 members of Tsongas' family gathered in the house to meet with friends Tuesday, said Nance Guilmarton, Tsongas' former press secretary and a family friend.
President Clinton, who defeated Tsongas for the Democratic nomination for president in 1992, called his widow Nicola on Monday to express his condolences, Guilmarton said.
Massachusetts senators Edward Kennedy and John Kerry were expected to return from Clinton's inauguration in Washington to pay their respects, she said.

After passing pictures of Tsongas with Kennedy, Kerry and former Mass. Gov. Michael Dukakis, well-wishers were ushered into a heated tent and past his closed casket. Services will be held at the Transfigural Greek Orthodox Church in Lowell on Thursday and Tsongas will be buried in the Lowell cemetery.
